doc.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Opening for Thelonious Monk at the Village Vanguard
summary: Monk talks to him in the kitchen dressing room about Charlie Christian and arriving in New York, and they later tour together.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: No, but that was another club that I liked too. We opened for him down at the Village Vanguard. He used to talk to me in the kitchen. That was the dressing room, really, the big kitchen they had.
Oh yeah, at the Vanguard, right.

He used to talk to me about Charlie Christian. He told me I was going to be the second Charlie Christian. Then he told me that when he came to New York, he was like Art Tatum. He said, “I was only 17 years old. I scared everybody to death.” That’s what he said. It was fun talking to him, because he was so different. But he was definitely a genius. I found that all those cats who had those weird reputations – “Oh, he’s crazy. Miles is crazy.” No, the one thing I know, Miles ain’t crazy. And Thelonious Monk? A genius. A crazy man can’t do what Thelonious Monk can do. I can tell you that. And when he’d talk – although sometimes he’d go off in a corner – he’d be talking about things you couldn’t possibly understand, because he was way ahead of everybody else. But he was exciting to talk to.
Did you get a chance to play with him? With Monk?
No. We went on tour together, though.
